title: Opening night at Eddie Condon's
summary: Condon's opens with Joe Marsala, Bud Freeman, Dave Tough and Gene Schroeder, who were hired for the night, and Tony Parenti plays the second night.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, anyway, then after you got out of the Army, you went back and you told about playing with Hodes and the other ones and the trio so far -- finally Condon's opened.
Yes - finally it opened.
And, that was just before the turn of the year - in 1946 - is that right?
How do I know? I don't know---
Well, whenever it was. Okay. Tell about---
I got out of the Army in 1945.
Tell about--- well, it took several months after you got out before Condon's---
I told you - I worked with Art Hodes.
Right - okay - now, uh, tell about the opening night at Condon's-- that was an historic evening
in jazz---

Well, I always thought it was very funny - the opening. Of course, we would never have a reshearsal the whole time I would visit Condon's. I was at Condon's twelve and a half years and we never rehearsed.
Yeah - not even for the opening night--
No - no - we just rehearsed on the bandstand; Condon called the tunes and we all knew them and we played them, but I thought it was very funny on opening night, we had Monty Marsala on the clarinet--
On the clarinet----
Yes.
You mean Joe.
Well, Joe - Joe Marsala. Joe was playing the clarinet and Bud Freeman played on tenor and, uh, Bob Casey and the great drummer that got killed in Brooklyn---
Dave Tough.
Dave Tough and, of course, (inaudible).
Old bludgeon foot--
Yes. I don't know whether it was Bob Casey or whether it was the guy with the gray hair now - bass player ---
Jack Lesberg---
Jack Lesberg--- I'm not sure about who was on it; it might have been Jack Lesberg.
Well, that's a long story which Lesberg can tell.
Yeah and it was Brad Gowans.
Casey was there about one day because Lesberg had to get another job.
Oh, is that it--
Yes.
Well, anyway, I must tell you about that; you know, we played that big opening night and my God, what a night ---
You had Gene Schrader on piano?
Yes. And, so, the second night, we had a different band. We had a different clarinet player ---
Everybody scattered.
No - it was just they hired those guys for opening night and, then, it was Tony Parenti I think that came in--
The second night.
The second night. And, of course, he had been with -- for years, he had been with Ted Lewis and it just--- that's the way the little thing got started.
I think Lesberg may have been there the second night or something like that.
Yes - could be because changes I thought was very strange (inaudible).
